maya: Observed two OOMs on prod-rt-03 during the 18:20 traffic spike. Looks like batch admission let three long-ctx requests into the same tile and kernel fallback increased KV footprint, pushing us over GPU memory.

eli: Can you paste the stack trace / logs? I saw similar on canary earlier.

maya: Logs:
```
[2025-06-19T18:20:12Z] batch_admit: accepted reqs=3 total_tokens=18240 kv_bytes=14.3GB gpu_free=800MB
[2025-06-19T18:20:13Z] kernel_fallback: switched to fallback-x64 kv_overhead=+3.2GB
[2025-06-19T18:20:13Z] OOM: process killed
```

eli: Profile snippet from profiler on same run:
```
GPU 0: model=A100-80GB runtime=triton kernel=fast_f32 -> fallback slow_q4
KV allocs: 11.8GB -> 15.0GB (+27%)
active_batches: 4  queued_tokens=2.7k
```

tess: Hypothesis: fallback increases per-request KV footprint by ~1MB/token for long contexts; batcher currently does token-budgeting based on mean seq len, not worst-case. We should add conservative headroom delta for kernels that can fallback.

devon: Proposal:
- compute token_budget = max(p50*1.3, p95)
- reserve kv_headroom = max(1.5GB, per_gpu_free*0.1)
- if kernel_switch_prob > 0.1, lower batch_size by 20%

maya: Simple admission patch I tested on canary: reduce admit if any req.seq_len > 4096 and gpu_free < 6GB. Prevents multi-long-ctx stacking. No perf regression on 95% lat.

build-bot: CI: batcher-test::admit_thresholds FAILED on staging (flaky) — see https://ci.redwood/4567

eli: Quick A/B: route long-ctx requests to low-kv kernel (quantized variant) while preferring fast kernel for short ones. That might shift latency but keeps OOMs down.

tess: Also add a metric: kv_headroom_fraction and kernel_fallback_rate per tile. We can alert when headroom < 12%.

devon: Action items:
- @eli add kernel_fallback_rate metric + dashboard (EOD)
- @maya push canary admit patch with unit tests (tomorrow)
- @tess wire kv_headroom_fraction alert (this week)

maya: sounds good. I'll also run a quick sim to model worst-case stacking probabilities and post numbers.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-1597 (OOM on prod-rt-03) assigned to maya & ops-team

maya: quick note: in sim, 3x long-ctx arriving within 200ms has ~0.8% daily probability at peak traffic — not huge but high-impact. Conservatively limiting multi-long admissions reduces expected daily OOM risk by ~95%.

devon: We'll keep kernel selection fallback logic but bias admission to avoid combos that trigger it. low-effort win.

eli: :+1: 

maya: I'll post canary results once patch lands.
